today.name: Cekura Bench
today.tagline: Speech-to-speech model benchmarks on live phone calls
today.description: Cekura Bench publishes voice AI benchmarks you can verify. Our new speech-to-speech benchmark tests 9 realtime voice models, including GPT Realtime 2.1, Gemini Live, Grok and Phonic, as complete phone agents on live calls: 82 scenarios, three runs each. Models are ranked on reliability, data accuracy, stalled calls, response time and cost, and every call transcript is public. Cekura Bench also covers voice agent benchmarks and STT benchmarks, with TTS benchmarks coming soon.

comments.text: Hi everyone, I am Sidhant from Cekura. Today we are launching our speech-to-speech benchmark. We ran 9 realtime voice models as the full agent inside the same open-source Pipecat phone agent, with the same prompt, tools and phone line. Each model handled 82 scenarios across a clinic booking flow and a Medicare intake, three times each. A call passes only if the agent reaches the right outcome and saves every field correctly. Results: Most reliable: GPT Realtime 2.1, 79.3% of scenarios passed on all three runs Fastest: Phonic v1, 1.60s median response Lowest cost: GPT Realtime 2.1 Mini, $0.020 per minute A cascade baseline (Flux, GPT-4.1, ElevenLabs Flash) scored 82.9%, above every realtime model Every call links to its transcript, tool calls and scores, and the agent and test cases are on GitHub. We would value your feedback, especially on which models we should add next.

week.name: Rill Browser
week.tagline: The browser where Claude Code and Codex work beside you
week.description: Rill is an AI-native browser built around the Claude Code and Codex you already use. Browse normally, then press ⌘E on any page to turn what you're looking at into a task for your agent. Rill finds the right project, passes along the context, and the agent works while you keep browsing. It also sorts your tabs into themes, turns your history into days you can search, and brings every project your agents are working on into one place. Free, on the plan you already have.

Then when an idea hit me, I'd have to stop, switch to coding agents, find the project and explain it all, and most of the time I just didn't.Rill is my way of removing that code-switching. It's a browser with your Claude Code or Codex working alongside you. When something on a page gives you an idea, you say so right there, and an agent starts on it in the right project. You don't have to spend time looking for the right folder, rephrasing everything you just saw on the web, and you don't switch in and out of work mode. The work goes on with you in the flow.This matters now more than ever. Agents have shortened the distance between ideas to output near zero. So the bottleneck is capturing the idea at the moment you have it. That moment is nearly always while you're taking something in, and that is what a browser is for.Rill is a free AI-native browser. It's WebKit-based, which means it's native to Mac. And it runs on the Claude Code or Codex plan you already have, so you don't have to buy a new subscription for all of its agentic capabilities.cHow do you keep an idea today when it shows up at the wrong time?

week.name: FastRouter.ai

week.description: FastRouter is a unified AI gateway and control plane for developers and enterprise teams building with LLMs. It routes every request to the right model across 200+ LLMs through one OpenAI-compatible API, optimizing for cost, latency, quality, and reliability. With intelligent routing, failover, observability, and governance, teams can scale AI apps without vendor lock-in or code changes.

Cost, latency and quality is three knobs where the third one does all the work and is the hardest to measure. So the number I'd want out of a control plane is cost per accepted output, not cost per call, because a model that's 4x cheaper and needs two regenerations just moved the bill somewhere nobody is measuring. week.aiReview: مسئله اصلی که Opengeni حل می‌کند، شکاف بین «ساختن یک دمو از هوش مصنوعی» و «اجرای پایدار آن در تولید» است. بسیاری از توسعه‌دهندگان می‌توانند یک Agent بسازند، اما مدیریت خطاها، احراز هویت، ایزوله‌سازی محیط اجرا و شفافیت هزینه‌ها چالش‌های بزرگی هستند. راه‌حل Opengeni یک لایه زیرساختی (Infrastructure Layer) است که این نگرانی‌ها را به عهده می‌گیرد و به توسعه‌دهندگان اجازه می‌دهد فقط روی منطق کسب‌وکار تمرکز کنند. از نظر معماری، این محصول بر پایه‌ی جلسات (Sessions) با قابلیت بازیابی از خطا (Recovery) و ساندباکس‌های ایزوله بنا شده است که امنیت و پایداری را تضمین می‌کند. مدل درآمدی ترکیبی از هزینه مدل‌های هوش مصنوعی به اضافه یک حاشیه سود کوچک (۵٪) است که برای توسعه‌دهندگان جذاب است زیرا هزینه پلتفرم ثابت ندارد. نقاط قوت اصلی شامل متن‌باز بودن (Open Source) برای خود میزبانی، یکپارچه‌سازی گسترده با ۱۰۰+ سرویس، و قابلیت ردیابی دقیق هزینه‌هاست. از سوی دیگر، نقاط ضعف احتمالی می‌تواند شامل پیچیدگی تنظیمات اولیه برای تیم‌های غیرفنی و وابستگی به کیفیت مدل‌های هوش مصنوعی پایه باشد. نکته طلایی برای ایران: با توجه به محدودیت‌های دسترسی به سرویس‌های ابری خارجی، ارائه نسخه‌ای از این پلتفرم که با مدل‌های هوش مصنوعی داخلی یا سرورهای محلی (Local LLMs) یکپارچه شده باشد، می‌تواند یک مزیت رقابتی عظیم ایجاد کند. همچنین، تمرکز بر «اعتمادسازی» (Trust) و شفافیت در هزینه‌ها برای بازار ایران که حساسیت بالایی به هزینه‌های پنهان دارد، بسیار حیاتی است.

week.name: AUDR by Chargebee
week.tagline: Open standard for tracking agent run costs
week.description: AUDR (Agent Usage Detail Record) is an open standard, for capturing who initiated an agent run and what it cost across every system that run touches. Inspired by the telecom industry's Call Detail Record, AUDR defines a common JSON schema that any harness, router, or billing system can emit and ingest. Three core rules make it work: a shared run ID minted by the harness, clear field ownership, and strict merge rules where conflicts are rejected and corrections are new records.

Full disclosure — I'm a big fan of Anthropic and actually built an app that works exclusively with Claude Desktop for secure local file search. So I've spent a lot of time thinking about this space.My concern with Cowork isn't the vision, it's the architecture. Agentic tasks burn through tokens fast (Anthropic says so themselves), so that $200/month cap can disappear quicker than you'd expect. And at that price, you'd want to use it for real work — but the whole thing requires giving Claude direct read/write/delete access to your files. If you're handling client data, patient records, or anything regulated, you're basically out.The bigger issue is prompt injection. Anthropic admits "the chances of an attack are still non-zero" — and back in October 2025, researchers showed exactly that: a prompt injection against Claude that pulled up to 30MB of user data per request through Anthropic's own API. When you're talking about an agent with file system access, email connectors, and a browser, that's not some theoretical edge case.There's a reason some of us build tools where Claude can search your files without actually touching them. The agentic future is definitely coming, but "AI that can access everything" and "AI that keeps you in control" are two very different products for two very different users.
